findings.issue: ConfigureStartUrl only checks path[0] == '/', which does NOT restrict --start-url to a relative in-app route. BlazorWebView.StartPath is resolved by WebViewManager as new Uri(appBaseUri, startPath), and a protocol-relative value escapes the app origin: [Uri]::new('https://0.0.0.1/','//evil.invalid/x') => 'https://evil.invalid/x'. Verified live on this machine: launching the built exe with --remote-debugging-port=9444 --start-url=//localhost:9600/probe caused an outbound TCP connection to a listener I opened on 127.0.0.1:9600 (proof the WebView2 left the app origin) and left the CDP target at url=about:blank with no Blazor app loaded, whereas the control run with --start-url=/w08 gave url=https://0.0.0.1/w08. An attacker who can supply the app's arguments (shortcut, launcher, another process) can therefore point the Blazor Hybrid WebView -- which carries the host-object/JS-interop bridge and the app's WebView2 profile -- at an arbitrary remote origin. The comment 'Not a rooted in-app path - ignore' claims a guarantee the code does not provide.
findings.fix: Tighten the guard in ConfigureStartUrl to reject authority-relative and backslash forms: replace 'if (path.Length == 0 || path[0] != '/')' with: if (path.Length == 0 || path[0] != '/' || (path.Length > 1 && (path[1] == '/' || path[1] == '\\')) || path.Contains('\\', StringComparison.Ordinal) || !Uri.TryCreate(path, UriKind.Relative, out _)) { continue; }  Re-verify with --start-url=//localhost:9600/probe: the flag must be ignored and the app must start on '/'.

findings.issue: W08ScreenshotDiff does not capture the viewport at 1366x768 as the spec requires, and the recorded percentage is host-DPI dependent. --window-size sets BlazorView.Width/Height in WPF DIPs, so the host display's raster scale leaks into the capture: the PNG produced by both runs here is 1709x960 (this display runs at 125% scaling), while the design export is 1366x768. ImageDiff then UPSCALES the design export to 1709x960, adding resampling noise on top of the real layout delta, so the 34.1035% figure is not reproducible on a machine with different display scaling -- which defeats the purpose of a harness B1-B8 will use for acceptance screenshots.
findings.fix: Pin the CSS viewport and device scale factor from the test instead of relying on the window size: var cdp = await page.Context.NewCDPSessionAsync(page); await cdp.SendAsync("Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride", new Dictionary<string, object> { ["width"] = 1366, ["height"] = 768, ["deviceScaleFactor"] = 1, ["mobile"] = false }); ... screenshot ... await cdp.SendAsync("Emulation.clearDeviceMetricsOverride"); Then W08-actual.png is exactly 1366x768, ImageDiff's resize path is never taken, and the percentage is machine-independent. Assert the captured size (e.g. Assert.Equal(1366, bitmap.Width)) so a regression is caught.

findings.issue: The launcher never checks that the CDP port is free before starting the app, and WakeelE2eFixture.WaitForPageAsync picks browser.Contexts.SelectMany(c => c.Pages).FirstOrDefault(). Verified live: two Wakeel.Desktop.exe instances share one WebView2 browser process (same fixed user-data folder) and therefore one CDP endpoint -- with instance A on --start-url=/w08 already running, starting instance B with --start-url=/gallery on the same --remote-debugging-port=9333 left BOTH alive and /json/list returned two page targets (https://0.0.0.1/gallery and https://0.0.0.1/w08). So after any aborted run (Ctrl+C, a crashed test host) that leaves a stale instance: /json/version answers instantly before the new instance is up, the fixture may bind to the stale page (page order across contexts is attach-ordered, not specified), and DisposeAsync kills only the process it started -- the stale one survives and every later run degrades further. That is exactly the determinism property this package is supposed to guarantee.
findings.fix: (a) In StartAsync, before Process.Start, issue one GET to http://127.0.0.1:{pollPort}/json/version and throw WakeelAppLaunchException if anything answers (message naming the leftover process), or enumerate and kill existing Wakeel.Desktop.exe processes first. (b) In WakeelE2eFixture.WaitForPageAsync, pass the expected start route and select the page whose Url path equals it (pages.FirstOrDefault(p => new Uri(p.Url).AbsolutePath == "/gallery")) instead of FirstOrDefault(), failing with the list of observed URLs on timeout.

findings.issue: ConfigureRemoteDebugging writes WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS only when a valid --remote-debugging-port flag is present. If the variable is already set in the inherited process environment, WebView2 still honours it, so remote debugging (and arbitrary extra Chromium switches such as --remote-allow-origins or --disable-web-security, which the flag path deliberately refuses to forward) can be enabled without any command-line flag. The stated property 'the port is only honoured when passed on the command line' is therefore not enforced by the app.
findings.fix: Clear the variable unconditionally at the top of ConfigureRemoteDebugging -- Environment.SetEnvironmentVariable("WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS", null); -- and only then set it for a validated port, so the inherited process environment can never contribute switches.

findings.issue: StartAsync has one path that starts Wakeel.Desktop.exe and never kills it: cancellation. http.GetAsync(versionUrl, cancellationToken) and Task.Delay(250, cancellationToken) throw OperationCanceledException straight out of the method with the process still running (only HttpRequestException/TaskCanceledException are handled, and a cancelled-token TaskCanceledException is swallowed by the polling branch so the loop spins until Task.Delay throws). The Process object is also never disposed (handle leak), including in DisposeAsync.
findings.fix: Wrap the polling loop in try { ... } catch { await KillAsync(process); throw; } so any exception kills the process before propagating, and add process.Dispose() after KillAsync in DisposeAsync.

findings.issue: W08ScreenshotDiff clicks the light-theme tab and never restores the previous choice, so it permanently leaves the developer's real %LocalAppData%\Wakeel\ui-state.json on "light" (ThemeToggles is careful to restore "system" in a finally; W08ScreenshotDiff is not). Confirmed: my runs left the persisted theme changed.
findings.fix: Either mirror ThemeToggles' finally block (click Ar.Gallery.ThemeSystem after the screenshot), or better, read the theme once in WakeelE2eFixture.InitializeAsync and restore it in DisposeAsync so every test in the assembly is covered in one place.

findings.issue: Assert.InRange(percentage, 0d, 100d) is a tautology: ImageDiff returns diffPixelCount * 100.0 / totalPixelCount, which cannot leave [0,100] by construction, so the assertion can never fail and gives false confidence that the diff step is verified.
findings.fix: Replace it with assertions on the artefacts the spec asks for: Assert.True(File.Exists(diffPath)) and Assert.Equal(percentage.ToString("F4"), File.ReadAllText(percentagePath)), keeping the _output.WriteLine recording as-is.

findings.issue: tests/Wakeel.E2E/artifacts/ is untracked and matched by no .gitignore rule, so the ~290 KB of PNGs regenerated by every test run (W08-actual.png, W08-diff.png, W08-diff-percentage.txt) will be committed by a plain 'git add -A' and re-diff on every subsequent run. Confirmed by git status --porcelain (?? tests/Wakeel.E2E/artifacts/).
findings.fix: Add a 'tests/Wakeel.E2E/artifacts/' line to .gitignore. Note .gitignore is outside this package's allowed edit paths, so this needs supervisor approval rather than a builder edit.

missing_spec_items: Spec 3 (W08ScreenshotDiff): 'screenshot the viewport at 1366x768' is not achieved -- the captured PNG is 1709x960 on this 125%-scaled display because the viewport is only set indirectly via WPF DIPs; the harness never pins the CSS viewport/deviceScaleFactor, so the acceptance screenshots B1-B8 will depend on are host-DPI dependent (and it is the design export, not the actual capture, that gets resampled).

Spec 1 (--start-url=/route, 'must start with /'): the intent 'only a relative app route' is not enforced -- protocol-relative values such as --start-url=//host/path pass validation and navigate the WebView2 to a foreign origin (demonstrated live).
notes:
Ran exactly the mandated commands twice from D:/AI/Administration2, reading full output.
Run 1: dotnet build src/Wakeel.Desktop -> 0 warnings/0 errors (5.7 s); dotnet build tests/Wakeel.E2E -> 0 warnings/0 errors (2.2 s); dotnet test tests/Wakeel.E2E --no-build -> Passed! Failed: 0, Passed: 4, Skipped: 0, Total: 4, Duration 13 s.
Run 2: identical -- 0 warnings/0 errors on both builds, 4/4 passed, 13 s. Warnings-as-errors is genuinely in force (Directory.Build.props TreatWarningsAsErrors=true, only CS1591 excluded) and the project is clean.
Measured W08 diff percentage: 34.1035% in both runs (tests/Wakeel.E2E/artifacts/W08-diff-percentage.txt), i.e. deterministic on this machine -- but see the medium DPI finding: it comes from upscaling the 1366x768 design export to the 1709x960 capture, so it is not portable to another display scaling.
No Wakeel.Desktop.exe was left behind after either run, nor after any of my manual probes (tasklist checked each time). I modified no file; git status is unchanged apart from the builder's own files and the regenerated artifacts.
Verified beyond reading: (1) the --start-url origin escape, proven with a loopback TcpListener on 127.0.0.1:9600 receiving the WebView2's connection, plus a control run showing /w08 resolves correctly to https://0.0.0.1/w08; (2) the two-instance CDP collision, proven by /json/list returning two page targets with both processes alive; (3) screenshot dimensions read straight from the PNG headers (actual 1709x960 vs expected 1366x768).
Correct and worth keeping: StartPath via BlazorWebView rather than a JS-injection hack; reading the origin back from the live page instead of hardcoding https://0.0.0.1; the AppLaunchTimeout test omitting --remote-debugging-port so CDP genuinely never opens and asserting ProcessWasKilled rather than merely that an exception was thrown; [assembly: CollectionBehavior(DisableTestParallelization = true)] (justified -- the shared WebView2 profile really is a single fixed path, as my two-instance probe confirms); the 30 s readiness poll on /json/version with a log tail from ProgramData and a LocalAppData fallback; kill-on-failure in InitializeAsync's catch as well as in DisposeAsync; no new NuGet package (System.Drawing via UseWindowsForms is a legitimate way to avoid one); ThemeToggles' token assertion is not tautological (tokens.css light --w-bg #F3F4F6 vs dark #121A1E, and both the attribute and the computed token are asserted) and GalleryOpens compares against Wakeel.Design.Text.Ar.Gallery.Title rather than a literal.
Non-findings I checked deliberately: --remote-debugging-port parsing is safe against switch injection (ushort.TryParse, non-zero, reformatted as an integer before being placed in the env var, process-scoped by default); --window-size parsing rejects garbage and is bounded (200..10000); build/e2e.ps1's Arabic comments/messages match the existing build/build.ps1 convention (ARCHITECTURE.md Sec.12's English rule applies to code, and all C# comments/XML docs here are English); ImageDiff's GetPixel/SetPixel loop is O(1.6M) per run but costs well under the observed 13 s; double DisposeAsync of the fixture (catch path plus xunit) is safe.
Unrelated observation, no action taken: two untracked Word files appeared at the repository root during this review ('نموذج المراسلة.docx' and its '~$' lock file), meaning Word has a document open there. Nothing to do with this package -- flagged only so they are not swept into its commit.
